sanskrit: kaccit te yāsyataḥ śatrūn pūrvaṃ yānti svanuṣṭhitāḥ sāma dānaṃ ca bhedaś ca daṇḍaś ca vidhivad guṇāḥ
english: Do the well-practised virtues — conciliation, gifts, sowing dissension, and chastisement — go before you when you march against enemies?

sanskrit: kaccin mūlaṃ dṛḍhaṃ kṛtvā yātrāṃ yāsi viśāṃ pate tāṃś ca vikramase jetuṃ jitvā ca parirakṣasi
english: O lord of the people, do you set out on campaign only after securing your base, strive to conquer your foes, and then protect what you have won?

sanskrit: kaccid aṣṭāṅgasaṃyuktā caturvidhabalā camūḥ balamukhyaiḥ sunītā te dviṣatāṃ pratibādhanī
english: Is your army, composed of the fourfold force and endowed with its eight constituents, well led by its generals so as to repel your enemies?

sanskrit: kaccil lavaṃ ca muṣṭiṃ ca pararāṣṭre paraṃtapa avihāya mahārāja vihaṃsi samare ripūn
english: O scorcher of foes, O great king, do you in battle destroy your enemies without leaving behind even the smallest gleaning or handful in a foreign kingdom?

sanskrit: kaccit svapararāṣṭreṣu bahavo 'dhikṛtās tava arthān samanutiṣṭhanti rakṣanti ca parasparam
english: Are many officials appointed by you in both your own and enemy kingdoms, who look after your interests and protect one another?

sanskrit: kaccid abhyavahāryāṇi gātrasaṃsparśakāni ca ghreyāṇi ca mahārāja rakṣanty anumatās tava
english: O great king, do those whom you have authorized guard against dangers from things that are eaten, that touch the body, and that are smelled?

sanskrit: kaccit kośaṃ ca koṣṭhaṃ ca vāhanaṃ dvāram āyudham āyaś ca kṛtakalyāṇais tava bhaktair anuṣṭhitaḥ
english: Are your treasury, granary, conveyances, gates, armoury, and revenues maintained by your loyal servants who have been consecrated with auspicious rites?

sanskrit: kaccid ābhyantarebhyaś ca bāhyebhyaś ca viśāṃ pate rakṣasy ātmānam evāgre tāṃś ca svebhyo mithaś ca tān
english: O lord of the people, do you first protect yourself from both internal and external dangers, and then protect your subjects from one another?

sanskrit: kaccin na pāne dyūte vā krīḍāsu pramadāsu ca pratijānanti pūrvāhṇe vyayaṃ vyasanajaṃ tava
english: Do they not publicly declare, in the morning hours, your expenditure incurred through vices such as drinking, gambling, gaming, and women?

sanskrit: kaccid āyasya cārdhena caturbhāgena vā punaḥ pādabhāgais tribhir vāpi vyayaḥ saṃśodhyate tava
english: Is your expenditure settled with half of your income, or with a quarter, or with three-quarters of the quarter-share?

sanskrit: kaccij jñātīn gurūn vṛddhān vaṇijaḥ śilpinaḥ śritān abhīkṣṇam anugṛhṇāsi dhanadhānyena durgatān
english: Do you repeatedly show favour with wealth and grain to your kinsmen, elders, the aged, merchants, artisans, and those who have taken refuge with you, especially those in distress?

sanskrit: kaccid āyavyaye yuktāḥ sarve gaṇakalekhakāḥ anutiṣṭhanti pūrvāhṇe nityam āyavyayaṃ tava
english: Are all your accountants and scribes employed in income and expenditure attending daily in the morning to your revenues and disbursements?

sanskrit: kaccid artheṣu saṃprauḍhān hitakāmān anupriyān nāpakarṣasi karmabhyaḥ pūrvam aprāpya kilbiṣam
english: Do you refrain from removing from their offices those who are experienced in affairs, who desire your welfare, and who speak what is pleasing, without first finding any fault in them?

sanskrit: kaccid viditvā puruṣān uttamādhamamadhyamān tvaṃ karmasv anurūpeṣu niyojayasi bhārata
english: O Bharata, having recognized men as superior, inferior, or middling, do you assign them to tasks befitting each?

sanskrit: kaccin na lubdhāś caurā vā vairiṇo vā viśāṃ pate aprāptavyavahārā vā tava karmasv anuṣṭhitāḥ
english: O lord of the people, are the greedy, the dishonest, the hostile, or those who have not yet attained experience in affairs excluded from your service?

sanskrit: kaccin na lubdhaiś caurair vā kumāraiḥ strībalena vā tvayā vā pīḍyate rāṣṭraṃ kaccit puṣṭāḥ kṛṣīvalāḥ
english: Is your kingdom not oppressed by the greedy, by thieves, by princes, by a feminine faction, or by yourself? Are the farmers prosperous?

sanskrit: kaccid rāṣṭre taḍāgāni pūrṇāni ca mahānti ca bhāgaśo viniviṣṭāni na kṛṣir devamātṛkā
english: In your kingdom, are there large tanks, full of water, distributed in every region, so that agriculture does not depend solely on rain?

sanskrit: kaccid bījaṃ ca bhaktaṃ ca karṣakāyāvasīdate pratikaṃ ca śataṃ vṛddhyā dadāsy ṛṇam anugraham
english: Do you ensure that the farmer does not lack for seed or food, and do you lend money as a favour at a hundred for one?

sanskrit: kaccit svanuṣṭhitā tāta vārttā te sādhubhir janaiḥ vārttāyāṃ saṃśritas tāta loko 'yaṃ sukham edhate
english: O dear one, is agriculture and trade properly maintained by honest men in your kingdom? For, O dear one, by trade and agriculture this world prospers happily.

sanskrit: kaccic chucikṛtaḥ prājñāḥ pañca pañca svanuṣṭhitāḥ kṣemaṃ kurvanti saṃhatya rājañ janapade tava
english: O king, are groups of five wise men, duly purified and installed, jointly ensuring the security of your realm?

sanskrit: kaccin nagaraguptyarthaṃ grāmā nagaravat kṛtāḥ grāmavac ca kṛtā rakṣā te ca sarve tadarpaṇāḥ
english: For the protection of your capital, are villages made as strong as cities, is the defence arranged as in a village, and are all these villages devoted to that purpose?

sanskrit: kaccid balenānugatāḥ samāni viṣamāṇi ca purāṇacaurāḥ sādhyakṣāś caranti viṣaye tava
english: Do former robbers, accompanied by troops and under proper supervision, patrol both the accessible and inaccessible parts of your territory?

sanskrit: kaccit striyaḥ sāntvayasi kaccit tāś ca surakṣitāḥ kaccin na śraddadhāsy āsāṃ kaccid guhyaṃ na bhāṣase
english: Do you treat women with kindness? Are they well protected? Do you not trust them blindly? Do you not disclose secrets to them?

sanskrit: kaccic cārān niśi śrutvā tat kāryam anucintya ca priyāṇy anubhavañ śeṣe viditvābhyantaraṃ janam
english: Having heard your spies at night, having deliberated upon what must be done, and having learned the state of those within your household, do you sleep enjoying pleasant things?

sanskrit: kaccid dvau prathamau yāmau rātryāṃ suptvā viśāṃ pate saṃcintayasi dharmārthau yāma utthāya paścime
english: O lord of the people, do you sleep during the first two watches of the night and then, rising in the last watch, contemplate dharma and artha?

sanskrit: kaccid darśayase nityaṃ manuṣyān samalaṃkṛtān utthāya kāle kālajña saha pāṇḍava mantribhiḥ
english: O knower of the right moment, O son of Pāṇḍu, do you daily show yourself adorned with ornaments to the people, rising at the proper hour together with your ministers?

sanskrit: kaccid raktāmbaradharāḥ khaḍgahastāḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ abhitas tvām upāsante rakṣaṇārtham ariṃdama
english: O subduer of enemies, do guards wearing red garments, with swords in hand and fully adorned, attend upon you on all sides for your protection?

sanskrit: kaccid daṇḍyeṣu yamavat pūjyeṣu ca viśāṃ pate parīkṣya vartase samyag apriyeṣu priyeṣu ca
english: O lord of the people, do you, after proper examination, act like Yama toward those who deserve punishment and fittingly toward those who deserve honour, whether they be disagreeable or agreeable to you?

sanskrit: kaccic chārīram ābādham auṣadhair niyamena vā mānasaṃ vṛddhasevābhiḥ sadā pārthāpakarṣasi
english: O son of Pṛthā, do you always ward off bodily ailments with medicines and discipline, and mental ailments by attending on the aged?

sanskrit: kaccid vaidyāś cikitsāyām aṣṭāṅgāyāṃ viśāradāḥ suhṛdaś cānuraktāś ca śarīre te hitāḥ sadā
english: Are physicians skilled in the eightfold system of medicine, who are friends and devoted to you, always present for the benefit of your body?

sanskrit: kaccin na mānān mohād vā kāmād vāpi viśāṃ pate arthipratyarthinaḥ prāptān apāsyasi kathaṃ cana
english: O lord of the people, do you never dismiss out of pride, delusion, or desire the plaintiffs and defendants who have come before you?

sanskrit: kaccin na lobhān mohād vā viśrambhāt praṇayena vā āśritānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ vṛttiṃ tvaṃ saṃruṇatsi ca
english: Do you refrain from blocking the livelihood of those who have sought your protection out of greed, delusion, misplaced confidence, or affection?

sanskrit: kaccit paurā na sahitā ye ca te rāṣṭravāsinaḥ tvayā saha virudhyante paraiḥ krītāḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Are the citizens and the inhabitants of your realm not in any way jointly alienated from you, having been bought over by enemies?

sanskrit: kaccit te durbalaḥ śatrur balenopanipīḍitaḥ mantreṇa balavān kaś cid ubhābhyāṃ vā yudhiṣṭhira
english: O Yudhiṣṭhira, is a weak enemy who is being pressed hard by a stronger power brought over by counsel, or a strong one by force, or each by means of both?

sanskrit: kaccit sarve 'nuraktās tvāṃ bhūmipālāḥ pradhānataḥ kaccit prāṇāṃs tvadartheṣu saṃtyajanti tvayā hṛtāḥ
english: Are all the foremost rulers of the earth devoted to you, and do those whom you have won over surrender their very lives in your cause?

sanskrit: kaccit te sarvavidyāsu guṇato 'rcā pravartate brāhmaṇānāṃ ca sādhūnāṃ tava niḥśreyase śubhā
english: Is honour paid by you, according to their merit, in all branches of learning to brahmins and virtuous persons for your own supreme good and auspiciousness?

sanskrit: kaccid dharme trayīmūle pūrvair ācarite janaiḥ vartamānas tathā kartuṃ tasmin karmaṃi vartase
english: Do you abide in the dharma rooted in the Veda, as it was practised by people of old, and do you strive to perform that duty likewise?

sanskrit: kaccit tava gṛhe 'nnāni svādūny aśnanti vai dvijāḥ guṇavanti guṇopetās tavādhyakṣaṃ sadakṣiṇam
english: Do brahmins eat tasty, wholesome, and meritorious food in your house under your oversight, along with proper gifts?

sanskrit: kaccit kratūn ekacitto vājapeyāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ puṇḍarīkāṃś ca kārtsnyena yatase kartum ātmavān
english: With a single-pointed mind and self-mastery, do you strive to perform sacrifices, Vājapeya rites in their entirety, and Pundarika rites completely?

sanskrit: kaccij jñātīn gurūn vṛddhān daivatāṃs tāpasān api caityāṃś ca vṛkṣān kalyāṇān brāhmaṇāṃś ca namasyasi
english: Do you bow in reverence to kinsmen, teachers, the aged, the gods, ascetics, sacred trees of good omen, and brahmins?

sanskrit: kaccid eṣā ca te buddhir vṛttir eṣā ca te 'nagha āyuṣyā ca yaśasyā ca dharmakāmārthadarśinī
english: O sinless one, is this understanding yours and this your conduct — one that promotes long life and fame and is guided by dharma, desire, and material welfare?

sanskrit: etayā vartamānasya buddhyā rāṣṭraṃ na sīdati vijitya ca mahīṃ rājā so 'tyantaṃ sukham edhate
english: For a king who lives by this understanding, his kingdom does not sink; having conquered the earth, he thrives in supreme happiness.

sanskrit: kaccid āryo viśuddhātmā kṣāritaś caurakarmaṇi adṛṣṭaśāstrakuśalair na lobhād vadhyate śuciḥ
english: Is a noble man of pure soul, though accused of theft, not put to death out of greed by those who are unskilled in examining evidence through the legal texts?

sanskrit: pṛṣṭo gṛhītas tatkārī tajjñair dṛṣṭaḥ sakāraṇaḥ kaccin na mucyate steno dravyalobhān nararṣabha
english: O bull among men, is a thief who has been questioned, seized, proven guilty by experts with good cause, not released out of greed for his wealth?

sanskrit: vyutpanne kaccid āḍhyasya daridrasya ca bhārata arthān na mithyā paśyanti tavāmātyā hṛtā dhanaiḥ
english: O Bharata, when a case is being judged, do your ministers, bribed with money, not misrepresent the interests of both the rich and the poor?

sanskrit: nāstikyam anṛtaṃ krodhaṃ pramādaṃ dīrghasūtratām adarśanaṃ jñānavatām ālasyaṃ kṣiptacittatām
english: Atheism, falsehood, anger, heedlessness, procrastination, not consulting the wise, sloth, and a restless mind —

sanskrit: ekacintanam arthānām anarthajñaiś ca cintanam niścitānām anārambhaṃ mantrasyāparirakṣaṇam
english: — pondering affairs alone, or deliberating with those ignorant of what is harmful, failing to begin what has been decided, and not guarding one's counsels —

sanskrit: maṅgalyasyāprayogaṃ ca prasaṅgaṃ viṣayeṣu ca kaccit tvaṃ varjayasy etān rājadoṣāṃś caturdaśa
english: — not performing auspicious rites, and addiction to sensual pleasures — do you avoid these fourteen royal faults?

sanskrit: kaccit te saphalā vedāḥ kaccit te saphalaṃ dhanam kaccit te saphalā dārāḥ kaccit te saphalaṃ śrutam
english: Are your Vedas fruitful? Is your wealth fruitful? Is your wife fruitful? Is your learning fruitful?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ vai saphalā vedāḥ kathaṃ vai saphalaṃ dhanam kathaṃ vai saphalā dārāḥ kathaṃ vai saphalaṃ śrutam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How indeed are the Vedas fruitful? How indeed is wealth fruitful? How indeed is a wife fruitful? How indeed is learning fruitful?

sanskrit: nārada uvāca agnihotraphalā vedā dattabhuktaphalaṃ dhanam ratiputraphalā dārāḥ śīlavṛttaphalaṃ śrutam
english: Nārada said: The Vedas bear fruit in the Agnihotra sacrifice; wealth bears fruit in what is given away and enjoyed; a wife bears fruit in pleasure and offspring; learning bears fruit in good character and conduct.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etad ākhyāya sa munir nāradaḥ sumahātapāḥ papracchānantaram idaṃ dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having declared all this, the sage Nārada of surpassing austerity then asked this further question of the righteous-souled Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca kaccid abhyāgatā dūrād vaṇijo lābhakāraṇāt yathoktam avahāryante śulkaṃ śulkopajīvibhiḥ
english: Nārada said: Are merchants who have come from afar for the sake of gain assessed the customs duty exactly as prescribed by those who live by collecting customs?

sanskrit: kaccit te puruṣā rājan pure rāṣṭre ca mānitāḥ upānayanti paṇyāni upadhābhir avañcitāḥ
english: O king, are the men honoured by you in the city and in the countryside bringing their goods without being deceived by tricks?

sanskrit: kaccic chṛṇoṣi vṛddhānāṃ dharmārthasahitā giraḥ nityam arthavidāṃ tāta tathā dharmānudarśinām
english: O dear one, do you always listen to the words of the aged who are well versed in dharma and artha, those who know the meaning of things and those who perceive dharma?

sanskrit: kaccit te kṛṣitantreṣu goṣu puṣpaphaleṣu ca dharmārthaṃ ca dvijātibhyo dīyate madhusarpiṣī
english: For the sake of dharma and artha, is honey and clarified butter given to the twice-born from the produce of your agricultural estates, cattle herds, and gardens of flowers and fruits?

sanskrit: dravyopakaraṇaṃ kaccit sarvadā sarvaśilpinām cāturmāsyāvaraṃ samyaṅ niyataṃ saṃprayacchasi
english: Do you regularly and properly provide tools and materials to all artisans at least every four months?

sanskrit: kaccit kṛtaṃ vijānīṣe kartāraṃ ca praśaṃsasi satāṃ madhye mahārāja satkaroṣi ca pūjayan
english: O great king, do you recognize work well done, do you praise the one who did it, and do you honour and worship him in the assembly of the good?

sanskrit: kaccit sūtrāṇi sarvāṇi gṛhṇāsi bharatarṣabha hastisūtrāśvasūtrāṇi rathasūtrāṇi cābhibho
english: O bull of the Bharatas, O master, do you study all the manuals — the manuals on elephants, on horses, and on chariots?

sanskrit: kaccid abhyasyate śaśvad gṛhe te bharatarṣabha dhanurvedasya sūtraṃ ca yantrasūtraṃ ca nāgaram
english: O bull of the Bharatas, are the treatise on the science of archery and the treatise on siege engines and city fortification constantly practised in your household?

sanskrit: kaccid astrāṇi sarvāṇi brahmadaṇḍaś ca te 'nagha viṣayogāś ca te sarve viditāḥ śatrunāśanāḥ
english: O sinless one, are all weapons, the Brahmā staff, and all the uses of poison known to you for the destruction of enemies?

sanskrit: kaccid agnibhayāc caiva sarpavyālabhayāt tathā rogarakṣobhayāc caiva rāṣṭraṃ svaṃ parirakṣasi
english: Do you protect your own kingdom from the danger of fire, from the danger of serpents and wild beasts, and from the disturbance caused by disease?

sanskrit: kaccid andhāṃś ca mūkāṃś ca paṅgūn vyaṅgān abāndhavān piteva pāsi dharmajña tathā pravrajitān api
english: O knower of dharma, do you protect like a father the blind, the dumb, the lame, the maimed, the friendless, and also the wandering ascetics?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etāḥ kurūṇām ṛṣabho mahātmā; śrutvā giro brāhmaṇasattamasya praṇamya pādāv abhivādya hṛṣṭo; rājābravīn nāradaṃ devarūpam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The great-souled bull of the Kurus, having heard these words of the best of brahmins, bowed at his feet in salutation and, filled with joy, the king spoke to Nārada of godlike form.

sanskrit: evaṃ kariṣyāmi yathā tvayoktaṃ; prajñā hi me bhūya evābhivṛddhā uktvā tathā caiva cakāra rājā; lebhe mahīṃ sāgaramekhalāṃ ca
english: "I shall act exactly as you have told me; for my wisdom has thereby grown still further." Having spoken thus, the king acted accordingly and gained the earth girdled by the ocean.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca evaṃ yo vartate rājā cāturvarṇyasya rakṣaṇe sa vihṛtyeha susukhī śakrasyaiti salokatām
english: Nārada said: A king who conducts himself thus in the protection of the four orders, having enjoyed great happiness here, attains to the same world as Indra.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca saṃpūjyāthābhyanujñāto maharṣer vacanāt param pratyuvācānupūrvyeṇa dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having duly worshipped him and been given leave by the word of the great sage, the dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira then spoke in orderly reply.

sanskrit: bhagavan nyāyyam āhaitaṃ yathāvad dharmaniścayam yathāśakti yathānyāyaṃ kriyate 'yaṃ vidhir mayā
english: O blessed one, you have spoken what is right and the proper determination of dharma. To the best of my ability and in accordance with what is proper, this rule is followed by me.

sanskrit: rājabhir yad yathā kāryaṃ purā tat tan na saṃśayaḥ yathānyāyopanītārthaṃ kṛtaṃ hetumad arthavat
english: What was to be done by kings of old, precisely that — there is no doubt — was done in a manner conforming to what is proper, well-reasoned, and purposeful.

sanskrit: vayaṃ tu satpathaṃ teṣāṃ yātum icchāmahe prabho na tu śakyaṃ tathā gantuṃ yathā tair niyatātmabhiḥ
english: O lord, we desire to walk in that righteous path of theirs; but it is not possible to walk it in exactly the same way as those self-disciplined ones did.

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa dharmātmā vākyaṃ tad abhipūjya ca muhūrtāt prāptakālaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā lokacaraṃ munim
english: Having spoken thus, the righteous-souled one honoured those words, and after a moment, seeing the sage who wanders through the worlds —

sanskrit: nāradaṃ svastham āsīnam upāsīno yudhiṣṭhiraḥ apṛcchat pāṇḍavas tatra rājamadhye mahāmatiḥ
english: — Nārada, seated at his ease — Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Pāṇḍu, of great mind, sitting near him in the midst of the kings, asked him:

sanskrit: bhavān saṃcarate lokān sadā nānāvidhān bahūn brahmaṇā nirmitān pūrvaṃ prekṣamāṇo manojavaḥ
english: "You always move, swift as thought, through the many and various worlds created of old by Brahmā, observing them all.

sanskrit: īdṛśī bhavatā kā cid dṛṣṭapūrvā sabhā kva cit ito vā śreyasī brahmaṃs tan mamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ
english: O brahmin, has any assembly hall like this one ever been seen by you anywhere, or one superior to this? Tell me, I am asking."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā nāradas tasya dharmarājasya bhāṣitam pāṇḍavaṃ pratyuvācedaṃ smayan madhurayā girā
english: Having heard this utterance of the dharma-king, Nārada replied to the son of Pāṇḍu with a smile, in a sweet voice:

sanskrit: mānuṣeṣu na me tāta dṛṣṭapūrvā na ca śrutā sabhā maṇimayī rājan yatheyaṃ tava bhārata
english: "O dear one, O king, O Bharata, I have not previously seen nor heard of any hall made of gems among humans equal to yours.

sanskrit: sabhāṃ tu pitṛrājasya varuṇasya ca dhīmataḥ kathayiṣye tathendrasya kailāsanilayasya ca
english: But I shall describe the hall of Yama, king of the ancestors, and of the wise Varuṇa, and of Indra, and of him who dwells on Kailāsa.

sanskrit: brahmaṇaś ca sabhāṃ divyāṃ kathayiṣye gataklamām yadi te śravaṇe buddhir vartate bharatarṣabha
english: I shall also describe the divine hall of Brahmā, free from all weariness — if your mind inclines to hear it, O bull of the Bharatas."

sanskrit: nāradenaivam uktas tu dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ prāñjalir bhrātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ taiś ca sarvair nṛpair vṛtaḥ
english: When thus addressed by Nārada, the dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira, with hands joined in reverence, surrounded by his brothers and by all those kings,

sanskrit: nāradaṃ pratyuvācedaṃ dharmarājo mahāmanāḥ sabhāḥ kathaya tāḥ sarvāḥ śrotum icchāmahe vayam
english: — the dharma-king of great mind — replied to Nārada thus: "Describe all those assembly halls; we desire to hear of them."
